notes: per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)

L1 oracle: luaparse 0.3.1 (MIT), a Lua parser library independent of tree-sitter, run as calibration/oracles/luaparse/luaparse_dump.js (luaVersion LuaJIT, Node as a bench instrument only): every definition with a range, 4,265 on 662 files, 0 parse errors. Tier B on the D2 precedent (JavaParser, Roslyn, PSI, php-parser): an independent syntactic parser, so L1 can be excellent and L2 at most good. The tier is a claim for Opus review, not a harness fact. The parser is independent; the scope (a definition is a function stored in a statically named slot) is the dialect author's rule, written in the oracle's README, so sym_recall 1 and sym_precision 1 show the queries implement that rule over 4,265 real definitions, not that no other rule is reasonable.

L2 oracle: the grammar's own queries/tags.scm (tree-sitter-grammars/tree-sitter-lua v0.5.0, MIT) run by py-tree-sitter 0.25.2 with tree-sitter-lua 0.5.0, tier C (D5, calibration/oracles/ts-tags), so L2 is capped at good. Its call pairs and the dialect's differ in attribution: upstream marks the whole table_constructor as the definition of its function-valued fields (a call written in a sibling field of a callback table such as pickers.new(opts, { prompt_title = .., attach_mappings = function .. end }) is paired with the first function field, 40 pairs on telescope's attach_mappings alone), and it has no definition for a string-keyed function or a t["k"] = function; the dialect pairs a call with the innermost function around it. call_recall .9845 (13,770 of 13,987 pairs), call_precision .9679 (13,770 of 14,227).

universal-ctags 6.2.1 (tier B) is an unscored cross-check, not the L1 oracle: it writes no end line for Lua (range_agreement unmeasurable, L1 capped at good) and reads by pattern, not by parse. Over the same 662 files it reads sym_recall .9197, sym_precision .9826, kind_agreement 1, signature_coverage 1 (4,191 of 4,557 definitions matched; the incumbent walker read .2617 on telescope.nvim in the baseline). Its 366 unmatched definitions: 228 are text tagged as a function (a variable assigned the result of a call whose argument is a function, `local ok, err = pcall(function() ... end)`; an immediately invoked function expression; a string or table value on a line containing the word function; `type(v) ~= "function"` tagged as `~`), 122 are bracketed slots ctags spells by their key expression (`decoder[TAG.INTEGER] = function` is `INTEGER]`, `["k"] = function` is `["k"]`), and 16 sit inside block comments.

grammar: tree-sitter-lua v0.5.0 (the tag the incumbent luaextract.go's binding pins, MIT, ABI 15, external scanner), lua.wasm.gz 64,669 bytes gzip (173,721 raw), 311 peak module pages, 0 faults, 3.58 MB/CPU-s. Kong/kong is measured as 3.9.2's kong/ tree (sparse checkout; its spec/ suite and fixtures are not read), telescope.nvim as v0.2.2; both subjects parse without an ERROR node.

lang-parity against luaextract (same subjects, luaparse for L1 and the tags oracle for calls): sym_recall .6642 -> 1, sym_precision 1 -> 1, kind_agreement 1 -> 1, range_agreement 1 -> 1, signature_coverage 0 -> 1, call_recall .7338 -> .9845, call_precision .9449 -> .9679, level none -> L2, no SourceKind lost (LuaFunction is the one kind); verdict MERGE (design section 11 step 2). The incumbent stopped at the first function_declaration (no nested function, no `x = function`, no table field) and recorded a callee's whole text (M.foo, self:bar); the dialect records the last identifier.

not extracted, on purpose: module tables and variables (`local M = {}`), table fields that do not hold a function, a function in a computed slot (`t[TAG.X] = function`, `{ [KEY] = function }`: 46 on Kong, 19 on telescope.nvim: no static name), the second and later variables of `local a, b = function.., function..` (the anchored pattern reads the first pair; none in the subjects), and the require graph (L3, a file-symbol strategy, not attempted).
